request.spec:
The header shows the signed-in user's crew total when a person with the user's name leads a
crew: the due-totals of the crews they lead, added up; nothing otherwise.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The header shows the signed-in user's crew total when a person with the user's name leads a
crew: the due-totals of the crews they lead, added up; nothing otherwise.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The header now shows the signed-in user's crew total, and all 4 acceptance tests pass in `bin/e2e`.

The new figure, "My crews due" (`my-crew-due-total`), sits next to "My due" and "My overdue". It finds the people whose name or alias matches the signed-in user's name, ignoring case and spaces at either end, the same way "My due" does. It then adds up the due-totals of the crews those people lead. If they lead no crew, it's blank.

This was a front-end change only, since crews and their due-totals already existed. The server, the stored data and the audit file are unchanged.

- **`features/crews/crews.ts`**: I moved the per-person due-total calculation here from `crews.slot.tsx` and added a shared `crewDueTotal`. The crew rows and the header now both use it, so the header can't drift from what the crew rows show.
- **`features/header/header.slot.tsx`**: works out and shows the new total.

One difference from "My due": if more than one person matches the user's name, "My due" uses only the first match, but the crew total counts crews led by any of them. The request says "a person with the user's name", so I read it that way. The tests don't cover this case.
